title: Model Context Protocol Specification 2025-11-25: Tools
central_claim: Tools may declare outputSchema; servers MUST return conforming structuredContent; clients SHOULD validate it and SHOULD validate tool results before passing them to the LLM.
cite_claim: The MCP spec makes output-schema conformance a server MUST and client-side validation only a SHOULD; it defines no semantic (value-level) checks. Reuses RESEARCH.md C26.
location: Data Types > Tool Result > Output Schema; Security Considerations item 2
quote: Servers **MUST** provide structured results that conform to this schema. Clients **SHOULD** validate structured results against this schema.
relevance: Defines the schema-only floor that fiks contracts extend; the baseline every gateway or SDK can at most implement.

title: Model Context Protocol Specification 2026-07-28 (latest): Tools
central_claim: Latest spec keeps the MUST/SHOULD output-schema rule, widens structuredContent to any JSON value, and adds that clients SHOULD follow $ref resolution rules when validating outputs.
cite_claim: As of the 2026-07-28 revision, structuredContent may be any JSON value conforming to outputSchema, and output validation remains a client SHOULD.
location: Tool Result > Structured Content; Output Schema; Security Considerations item 2
quote: This can be any JSON value (object, array, string, number, boolean, or null) that conforms to the tool's `outputSchema` if one is defined.
relevance: C26 cites 2025-11-25; the paper should cite the current revision and note the change (object -> any JSON value).

title: MCP TypeScript SDK: Client.callTool structured-output validation
central_claim: The official TS client automatically validates structuredContent against a tool's cached outputSchema and throws if it is missing or non-conforming.
cite_claim: The reference TypeScript client rejects results whose structuredContent is absent or fails the declared outputSchema; it performs no value-level checks.
location: dist/esm/client/index.js lines 475-498 in sdk 1.32.0 (installed in fiks node_modules); packages/client/src/client/client.ts ~line 2498 on main
quote: Calls a tool and waits for the result. Automatically validates structured output if the tool has an outputSchema.
relevance: Runnable schema-only baseline (B1) at zero cost: add outputSchema to shop-mcp and count which drifts the stock client catches.

title: MCP Python SDK: ClientSession.validate_tool_result
central_claim: The Python client revalidates every non-error CallToolResult against the declared output schema with jsonschema and raises RuntimeError on mismatch.
cite_claim: The reference Python client also enforces outputSchema conformance on non-error results, raising on missing or invalid structuredContent.
location: src/mcp/client/session.py, call_tool and validate_tool_result (~lines 1100-1150 on main, read 2026-10-21)
quote: Revalidate a `CallToolResult` against the tool's declared output schema.
relevance: Second schema-only reference point; shows schema validation is commodity in both official SDKs.

title: docker mcp gateway run (CLI reference)
central_claim: Docker MCP Gateway ships interceptors, secret blocking and call logging (both on by default), signature verification and network blocking.
cite_claim: Docker MCP Gateway's built-in output-side controls are secret blocking and call logging; no schema or semantic output validation is documented.
quote: Block secrets from being/received sent to/from tools
relevance: Representative security-first gateway; feature-matrix row.

title: docker/mcp-gateway: Types of Interceptors (examples/interceptors README)
central_claim: exec, docker and http interceptors can run before or after a tool call; after-interceptors receive the tool response as JSON and may return a replacement.
cite_claim: Docker's open-source gateway exposes a post-call hook that receives the full tool response, so a contract checker can be plugged in without a custom proxy.
quote: Those which run run `after` have access to the tool call response.
relevance: Portability baseline B3: run fiks contract checks as an after:exec interceptor; also the strongest 'observe is not novel' counter-argument.

title: AI MCP Proxy plugin
central_claim: Protocol bridge between MCP and HTTP with ACLs, audit log and metrics; structured output and guardrails on MCP requests/responses are listed as not supported; Enterprise-only.
cite_claim: Kong's AI MCP Proxy explicitly does not support structured output or guardrails on MCP requests and responses.

central_claim: APIM exposes REST APIs or existing MCP servers as MCP; governance via rate limits, JWT auth, IP filtering, caching; monitoring via Azure Monitor/App Insights.

relevance: Cloud gateway row; proprietary, not runnable locally as a baseline.

title: Monitor MCP Server Traffic in Azure API Management
central_claim: APIM logs per-tool telemetry with gen_ai.* attributes; results only with opt-in payload logging; policies at MCP scope must not read the response body because MCP responses stream.

quote: Validates tool args and results against a minimal JSONSchema-like subset (type, properties, required).
